_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in moderate to severe plaque psoriasis; subjects received secukinumab 150 mg or 300 mg SC at Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3 followed by monthly maintenance.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with chronic plaque-type psoriasis for ≥6 months, PASI ≥12, IGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects achieving PASI 75 response at Week 12 and IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 12 (300 mg): PASI 75 200 (82%) vs placebo 11 (4%); IGA 0/1 160 (65%) vs placebo 6 (2%); PASI 90 145 (59%) vs placebo 3 (1%). Both secukinumab doses superior to placebo (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with an active comparator (EU-sourced etanercept); secukinumab 150 mg or 300 mg SC at Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3 followed by monthly maintenance.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with chronic plaque-type psoriasis, PASI ≥12, IGA ≥3, BSA ≥10% at baseline.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: proportion of subjects achieving PASI 75 response at Week 12 and IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1306 (300 mg N=327, 150 mg N=327, Placebo N=326, Etanercept N=326)
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 12 (300 mg): PASI 75 249 (76%) vs placebo 16 (5%) vs etanercept 142 (44%); IGA 0/1 202 (62%) vs placebo 9 (3%) vs etanercept 88 (27%). Secukinumab superior to placebo (p<0.0001) and superior to etanercept (p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>1%) are nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, and upper respiratory tract infection. In placebo-controlled trials nasopharyngitis occurred in 11.4% (300 mg, N=691) vs 8.6% placebo, upper respiratory tract infection 2.5% vs 0.7%. Infections were reported in 28.7% of COSENTYX subjects vs 18.9% placebo; serious infections in 0.14%.
target_moa: Human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-17A and inhibits its interaction with the IL-17 receptor, interrupting the inflammatory processes of psoriasis.

rems.type: No REMS required; the applicant voluntarily submitted a REMS (communication plan) but DRISK concluded the risk of infection can be effectively communicated via labeling and recommended no REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Drugs Advisory Committee convened October 20, 2014; committee unanimously agreed the data support approval.
